numerical_stability.classification: Numerical stability policy, not hardware physical properties.
numerical_stability.derivation: 0.004 / 0.0005 = 8. A timestep-only rest experiment passed K2b at 0.0005 s while 0.004 s failed with identical physical parameters.
numerical_stability.execution: Evaluate the frozen probe controller once per 0.004 s; hold its force command over eight native physics steps. Recompute native gamepad forces and constraints at each physics step.
numerical_stability.validation_scope: Selected from fixed/free no-contact response and timing comparisons. Full SDF contact validation and timestep convergence for this combination remain unverified; exact 23-degree non-penetration is unsupported.
numerical_stability.uncertainty_reason: This is a numerical policy, not hardware data. First boundary crossing remains about 0.35 degrees in the measured component experiment.
numerical_stability.approval_source: Owner instruction, 2026-10-20: adopt the tested discrete damping-ratio-5 combination.

contact_response.classification: Numerical contact policy, not measured material properties.
contact_response.scope: Gamepad collision geoms only. The acceptance probe uses native default solref and solmix. Caller geoms and global options are unchanged.
contact_response.priority_policy: Keep native geom priority unchanged; different priorities, explicit pairs, global overrides and direct-format solref retain native precedence.
contact_response.mixing_formula: Equal priority and positive solref: tau_eff = (w_pad*tau_pad + w_other*tau_other)/(w_pad+w_other). solimp uses the same weights. Friction uses element-wise maxima independently of solmix.
contact_response.weight_derivation: For default other tau=0.02 s and w=1, relative dilution <=1e-5 requires w_pad>=899999. Choose 1000000; tau_eff=0.002000017999982 s.
contact_response.uncertainty_reason: Trial numerical response; downstream validation, convergence and full-suite results are separate evidence, not hardware contact calibration.

sdf.classification: Numerical geometry representation policy, not hardware physical properties.
sdf.approval_source: Owner ruling 6, 2026-10-17: native SDF is the default; CoACD is an explicit comparison.
sdf.scope: One native SDF mesh per common triangle shell. Mesh depth is set through MjSpec before compilation. Search options are set only on standalone/acceptance models; caller options are preserved.
sdf.derivation: Select depth 8 before acceptance: a roughly 0.15 m shell has nominal finest-cell scale 0.15/2**8 = 0.000586 m (native depth 6 gives 0.002344 m). This is not an error bound or an equivalence to SAPIEN voxel spacing. Keep native search defaults 10 iterations and 40 initial points.

evidence.native_support: build/experiments/mb_m1/official_core.md section 4 and native SDF cavity experiment

sdf.uncertainty_reason: Octree depth controls representation, not a certified surface-distance error. Contact accuracy and timestep convergence are measured separately.

limit_response.classification: Numerical limit-response policy, not hardware physical properties.
limit_response.approval_source: Owner instruction: adopt the tested discrete damping-ratio-5 combination.
limit_response.scope: Circular shaft-limit spatial tendons only. Range, sites, zero margin, ReturnLaw, scalar click limits and geom contact parameters are unchanged.
limit_response.required_numerical_settings: The measured response uses discrete, refsafe disabled, Newton with 100 iterations and 1e-8 tolerance, diagexact disabled, and physics dt=0.0005 s. Attachment never edits caller global options.
limit_response.derivation: Selected tested candidate: strong native response, damping ratio 5, and maximum native impedance 0.9999. Reduces repeated rebound without a material cost increase relative to ratio 1 in the no-contact fixture. These are not measured spring/damping properties.
limit_response.uncertainty_reason: First crossing remains about 0.35 degrees. Exact non-penetration, other loading directions, full contact behavior and timestep convergence are not established by the component experiment.
